outcome.final_claim: 25/63 correlations significant at p<0.05 uncorrected on all 386 subjects, against ~3.2 expected from noise alone. Excluding 85 subjects flagged by infreq leaves 11/63 significant on n=301, so 14 associations do not survive quality control.
limitations: 63 uncorrected tests at alpha=0.05 -- roughly 3.2 false positives expected even under the null.
metrics_data: failed at least one infrequency (attention-check) item -- the study's own criterion (direct, 85 flagged).
survey_data: bottom-decile response variability across 54 survey items (straight-lining) (proxy, 41 flagged).
task_data: performing at or below chance across the whole task, or responding faster than the screen can be read (proxy, 171 flagged).
Against the study's own attention checks the exclusion rule has precision 1.0 and recall 1.0 (85 subjects truly careless) -- it is the criterion itself.
outcome.resolving_measurement: An attention check for every participant would settle inclusion directly; pre-registering which of the 63 correlations is the hypothesis would separate signal from the ~3 expected false positives.
